lead: Arlington sits between Dallas and Fort Worth, with a big mix of 1970s to 1990s homes and apartments. Hail, slab leaks and freeze-burst pipes cause most of its water damage.
risk: hail roof damage, slab leaks and frozen pipes
why: The median Arlington home was built in 1986. Many of those houses now have original water heaters, supply lines and roofs near the end of their life. They sit on slabs over clay soil that swells in wet weather and shrinks in drought. That movement stresses pipes under the floor. A slab leak may show up as a warm spot, cracked tile or a water bill that keeps climbing.

Weather adds sudden losses. North Texas spring storms bring large hail that cracks shingles and skylights, and leaks follow with the next rain. The February 2021 freeze burst pipes in attics and outside walls across the city. Arlington also has many apartments near UT Arlington and the Entertainment District, where a leak in one unit can spread to the next.
image_alt: Roofer using a nail gun on new shingles
image_caption: North Texas hail often leads to roof and ceiling leaks in Arlington homes.
tips: Get a roof check after hail, even if you see no leak.
Water the soil around the slab evenly during drought.
Insulate attic pipes and drip faucets on hard freeze nights.
Renters: report leaks to management in writing right away.
areas: Calls come from Downtown Arlington, the Entertainment District, Viridian, North Arlington, East Arlington, Southwest Arlington, Lake Arlington and the UT Arlington area, plus Grand Prairie, Mansfield and Pantego.

faq.q: Does insurance cover a slab leak in my Arlington home?
faq.a: Many policies cover the water damage from a sudden slab leak, plus the cost to access the pipe. They often do not cover the pipe repair itself or damage from a slow leak over time. Read your policy and file quickly once you find a leak.
